thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT P1 — serving-runtime eu-west: sudden spike in OOMs + CUDA driver resets, pods CrashLoopBackOff. PagerDuty  -> oncall.
amanda: I'm oncall. seeing repeated nv_gpu OOMs on 4 nodes, kernel messages about driver reset. pod logs show `tensorflow/cuda: cuMemoryAlloc failed` and then container restart.
amanda: autoscaler started adding nodes ~03:12 UTC but pods immediately crash, then scale-down fires, causing a rapid scale up/down loop. looks like thrash causing brownout on serving fleet. :fire:
maria: adding logs snippet
maria: ```
$ kubectl -n serving get pods -o wide | grep crash
serving-abc-1  CrashLoopBackOff  2/5  10m  node-42
...
$ kubectl logs serving-abc-1 -c runtime
E tensorflow: failed to allocate memory: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
E  -> driver reset, exiting
```
leo: autoscaler events:
leo: ```
I0312 03:11:56 autoscaler.go: scale up to 8 nodes
I0312 03:12:22 pod-controller: pod crashed, eviction
I0312 03:12:35 autoscaler.go: scale down to 3 nodes (stabilization window passed)
I0312 03:13:05 scale up to 7 nodes
```
leo: that pattern makes the nodes churn; pods' init/kv-cache warmups never finish.
sandeep: I'm paged, taking over — standby 2m.
amanda: handing off: context -> heavy model load from new rollout at 03:09, increased batch size + new CUDA kernel path enabled in runtime; we've cordoned node-42/43 and restarted runtime on node-41. disabled new canary traffic via routing rule.
amanda: actions so far: cordoned bad nodes, reduced batch_size to 1 for in-flight routes, scaled down canary pods, filed PD alert.
sandeep: plan (quick): 1) disable cluster-autoscaler scale-down 2) bump autoscaler stabilization window to 10m 3) revert runtime kernel change or pin to older op-kernel 4) activate region fallback routing to us-east for heavy models. executing 1 now.
sandeep: ```
# disable scale down
kubectl -n kube-system edit configmap cluster-autoscaler
# set scaleDownEnabled: false
```
maria: I'll switch heavy models to quantized fallback (q4_0) and apply per-route concurrency cap. doing model swap on 2 routes now.
maria: ```
curl -X POST $API/route/patch -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","model":"gptx-q4_0","concurrency":1}'
```
leo: also temporarily increase kubelet eviction threshold -> `--eviction-hard=memory.available<200Mi` not ideal but may stop immediate kills. proposing to patch daemonset on affected nodes.
deploy-bot: rollback of rollout/serving-runtime v2024.03.09 -> v2024.03.02 completed (commit abc123). :white_check_mark:
sandeep: after disabling scale-down and rollback, node count stabilized. no new OOMs in last 6m. metrics: tail latency improved, 95p latency down from 5.2s -> 1.1s.
amanda: customer impact snapshot: ~12-18% increase in 500s across hosted API at peak. Affected customers (observed increased errors): Mediq-API, AcmeSearch, Queryly. No SLA breach yet but user-visible errors for some endpoints. drafting status page note.
leo: follow-ups: run job to scan for kernels that use > allocated GPU mem, add runtime guard to fall back when mem alloc fails, add a canary traffic ramp (10% -> 50%) delay.
sandeep: mitigation status: autoscaler scale-down disabled, rollback in place, model fallback active, node cordons in effect. monitoring for 30m. marking as mitigated but degraded. :eyes:
infra-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> service degraded. Routing fallback active to us-east for heavy workloads. Incident channel will remain open for postmortem assign and customer comms.
amanda: will send targeted emails to affected accounts and add to status page. assigning postmortem to leo + maria, owner: leo. estimated write-up due EOD tomorrow.
deploy-bot: note: a hotfix branch created to add a safe-guard that rejects loads that request > configured reserved_gpu_memory. PR: github.com/redwood/serving/pull/987
amanda: thanks team. if thrash resumes -> escalate infra pager and consider temporary quota caps on free tier. I'll update the incident ticket and close after 1h stable.
sandeep: confirming last_message: 03:20 UTC — no new OOMs, node pool stable.
infra-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated -> monitoring) at 03:30 UTC. Postmortem scheduled. :memo:
